requirements.requirement: The system must ingest raw rating records from multiple sources conforming to the schema defined in EVAL-P5-S1.
The system must normalize all rating values to a common scale (0–100) regardless of original source scale.
The system must correctly convert ratings from at least 1–5 and 1–10 scales into the normalized scale.
The system must apply a recency weighting function that increases influence of more recent ratings over older ones.
The system must apply a volume weighting factor such that providers with more ratings have more stable scores.
The system must compute a single composite reputation score per provider based on normalized, weighted inputs.
The system must associate all ratings with providers using a valid NPI identifier.
The system must exclude ratings records that lack required fields (rating value, source, timestamp, NPI) from aggregation.
The system must handle missing ratings for a provider by returning a null or default score with a fallback indicator.
The system must apply fallback logic for sparse data (below minimum rating count threshold) to reduce score volatility.
The system must log all normalization and aggregation steps for traceability and auditability.
The system must ensure deterministic output such that identical inputs produce identical composite scores.
The system must use an LLM-assisted normalization mapping only when source scale metadata is ambiguous or missing.
The system must ensure LLM outputs for normalization are constrained to numeric scale mappings and not free-text responses.
The system must validate LLM-generated normalization outputs against predefined bounds before applying them.
The system must fall back to deterministic normalization logic if LLM output is invalid or unavailable.
The system must ensure LLM-assisted weighting suggestions do not override configured weighting rules without validation.
The system must limit LLM usage to non-critical augmentation paths and not core score computation.
The system must handle ingestion failure from one source without blocking aggregation from other available sources.
The system must return an error state when all input sources fail or no valid ratings are available.
